subject: Commitment rubric and smoke vignettes for trial acceptance
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Parker <elena.parker@careleaf.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commitment rubric and smoke vignettes for trial acceptance

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time last week. As discussed, I attached a first-pass mutual action plan (MAP) and a small set of smoke vignettes that articulate what success looks like for the 8-week trial. Key asks here:

- Review the acceptance rubric (tab: "Exit Signals") and confirm the tolerance thresholds for precision and latency.
- Identify the internal owners for the three acceptance tests (accuracy, latency, integration resilience).
- Let us know any procurement/contract timings we should reflect in the timeline.

High-level summary from our side:
- Acceptance gates: two critical gates (Safety & Accuracy) plus one operational gate (SLA sampling). All three must pass for go/no-go.
- Acceptance tests: 1) Concordance test against your labeled dataset (target: >= 92% top-1), 2) End-to-end P95 latency under 300ms for 90% of test prompts, 3) End-to-end failover and KV-cache resilience with zero data leakage.

Attachments: CareLeaf_MAP_v0.3.xlsx (MAP with milestones), smoke_vignettes.csv (20 representative prompts), eval-acceptance-matrix.pdf (print-friendly).

Proposed next steps: you confirm owners and any tweaks to thresholds, we lock the MAP and schedule the first integration week (Week 0).

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference

From: Elena Parker <elena.parker@careleaf.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@careleaf.com>, CareLeaf Procurement <procurement@careleaf.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2027 12:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commitment rubric and smoke vignettes for trial acceptance

Jonas —

Appreciate the level of detail. Quick notes after a first pass:

- Criteria: the 92% top-1 concordance looks reasonable for now but we need a "minimum viable" fallback threshold (e.g., 88%) to drive cutover behavior — can the MAP include a staged acceptance (88% pass enables limited pilot; 92% enables full commit)?
- Latency: 300ms P95 is aggressive for our mix of prompts. Can we adjust to P95 < 350ms with a P99 < 700ms SLO during the trial, with a plan to optimize to 300ms by production?
- Security/ops: procurement asked for a short evidence pack (SOC 2 scoping + access logs sampling cadence) — procurement copied here.

Owners:
- Accuracy verification: Tom Liu (Data Science)
- Integration & latency run: Ben Carter (Engineering) — Ben is on the email chain separately; I looped procurement instead of Ben to keep pri list clean.
- Executive signoff: me + Head of Clinical Ops (TBD)

We’ll review the MAP internally and get back with concrete owner names and procurement windows by Friday.

Thanks,
Elena Parker
Director of Product, CareLeaf Health
elena.parker@careleaf.com

Subject: Re: Commitment rubric and smoke vignettes for trial acceptance

Elena —

Thanks for the quick feedback, that staged acceptance approach makes sense and is straightforward to represent in the MAP. I updated the comments in the sheet and attached a one-pager flow in the body below to keep the email thread lightweight.

Proposed staged acceptance (concise):
- Phase A (Limited pilot): concordance >= 88% AND P95 latency < 350ms -> enable 1k DAU simulated; manual signoff by Data Science.
- Phase B (Full trial / commit readiness): concordance >= 92% AND P95 latency < 300ms AND pass SLA sampling -> executive signoff for commit.

Acceptance test owners (proposed):
- Accuracy verification: Tom Liu (CareLeaf) + Marissa Cole (Redwood QA)
- Latency and resilience: Ben Carter (CareLeaf eng) + Karthik Iyer (Redwood infra)
- Security evidence: Procurement (CareLeaf) pickup; Karthik will own evidence collection with our security team.

Small note on procurement windows: Marissa, can you confirm if a signature/PO timeline of 3 weeks after Phase B signoff aligns with our standard on Dedicated deals? If procurement requires additional contracting steps (e.g., addendum for data residency), we should call that out in the MAP timeline.

If everyone is aligned, I'll update the MAP to reflect the staged criteria and push a fresh version to the shared Drive link. Also happy to run a 30-minute working session with Tom + Ben + Karthik to align the test harness by Friday.

— Jonas

Date: Wed, 6 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commitment rubric and smoke vignettes for trial acceptance

Thanks all — short operational summary and next operational steps from Redwood infra/security perspective.

Operational summary (what we will validate during the 8-week engagement):
1) Accuracy: run concordance suite (20k labeled prompts) provided by CareLeaf. Output: pass/fail + confusion matrix. Lead: Tom Liu (CareLeaf) / Marissa Cole (Redwood QA).
2) Performance: staged load tests (1k DAU simulated for Phase A; 10k DAU for Phase B). We will produce P95/P99 latency distributions and a SLA sampling report. Lead: Ben Carter (CareLeaf) / myself.
3) Resilience & fallback: periodic KV-cache eviction tests and simulated GPU node failover to validate no token loss and consistent outputs. Lead: Karthik Iyer (Redwood infra).
4) Security evidence: SOC 2 scoping doc and 72-hr access log samples to be delivered within 5 business days of Phase A start. Lead: Karthik Iyer (Redwood secops).

Deliverables & timeline (proposed):
- Day 0: MAP locked, test harness access granted, sample dataset ingestion.
- Week 1: Phase A runs (limited pilot) + initial concordance and latency report.
- Week 3: Optimization sprint and follow-up load tests.
- Week 5: Phase B run for production-readiness verification.
- Week 6: Final evidence pack delivered for procurement and exec signoff.

Action items:
- Elena/Tom: confirm dataset drop and owner for clinical-sample tagging (by Fri EOD).
- Procurement: send any mandatory contract addendum requests (data residency/KMS) so we can surface in MAP.
- Marissa: confirm PO/signature lead time for Dedicated offering and whether 3-week target is achievable.

Attachments: eval-acceptance-matrix.pdf (compact checklist).

I can run the working session with Tom/Ben on Friday 10–10:30 PT to walk through load-test scaffolding and the smoke vignettes. Jonas — let me know if Friday works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure and Security
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com | +1 (650) 555-0231
